canvas-01.description: Sheet 64 of the 1907 New Jersey coast volume shows the northern end of Monmouth Beach, the narrow strip between the South Shrewsbury River and the Atlantic Ocean, drawn at 120 feet to an inch. Ocean Avenue runs up the right side of the sheet with large summer cottages and estates on its ocean side, among them the Storm Estate, J. E. Ewing and the Green Inn, and on its land side the Horton Cottages and the cottages of R. Lesher and Gilbert. Railroad Avenue follows the east side of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which crosses the sheet from top to bottom; a small station building near the middle is marked Galilee Station. Park Road and Central Road cross between Railroad and Ocean Avenues, and Central Road continues west to Monmouth Avenue, with W. H. Hamilton's house in the corner and the Prentiss Cottage on the open ground to the north. At the top the U.S. Life Saving Station boat house, the De Forest wireless station and a light station stand near Ocean Avenue. On the river side a spur curves to a row of numbered ice houses with a shed and boat houses along the shore. Much of the left half is open water of the South Shrewsbury River, with a compass rose; Cottage Road and another Park Road appear at the foot. A small key map of Monmouth Beach in the top left corner, showing sheets 61 and 64 to 67, is not part of this map. Block numbers 157 to 159 are printed.
notes: Railroad Av. is today's Seaview Avenue; Monmouth Av. is today's River Avenue.

The sheet does not agree with the modern streets within about 9 m: Park Road is drawn at a steeper angle than today's, and the drawing is a few percent larger than its 120 ft scale. Placed from one detected junction, three hand-picked junctions and two points carried from sheet 65; low confidence.
The railroad (Central R.R. of N.J., Sea Bright branch) has been removed.
Ocean Avenue and the shore have moved since 1907; the houses east of Ocean Avenue are largely gone.

Printed sheet 64 (N.J. Coast vol. 1), Monmouth Beach north end, scale 120 ft to an inch. Ocean Av., Railroad Av. (now Seaview Avenue), Park Rd., Central Rd., Monmouth Av. (now River Avenue), Cottage Rd. at the foot; South Shrewsbury River to the west. Top-left key map of Monmouth Beach (sheets 61, 64-67) is a small-scale index, masked out. One part.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 65 shows the centre of Monmouth Beach at 120 feet to an inch, from Cottage Road at the top to Conover Road at the foot and from Park Road (Gull Street) on the left to the Atlantic Ocean on the right. Ocean Avenue and Railroad Avenue run down the right half on either side of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, whose passenger station stands on Railroad Avenue; between them and along the shore are large cottages, named for owners such as W. Barbour, Fenshaw, J. B. Wilson, Nile, G. F. Baker, Potts, E. Groesbeck, Spaulding, Walton and McNally, with a bath house on the beach and the Country Club at Beach Road. The centre of the sheet holds the Monmouth Beach Club House inside Club House Circle, with River Drive and River Avenue running south past it and the M. H. Houghton club house stables, and houses of Prentice, Fargo, Jackson, Barrows, A. Symington, Thornall and Kellogg on the private drives to the north. Beach Road runs west to the village around Fresh Pond Road, where the Church of the Precious Blood, the Monmouth Beach Fire Department hose cart house, a livery, a garage and a wagon house stand among small dwellings. A pond lies at the lower left. Surf Road curves from Railroad Avenue to Ocean Avenue, and Conover Road leaves Ocean Avenue at the foot. Block numbers 145 to 156 are printed.
notes: Renamed since: Railroad Av. is Seaview Avenue; Monmouth Av., River Drive and River Av. together are River Avenue; Club House Circle is Club Circle; Park Rd. (Gull St.) is West Street; Fresh Pond Rd. is Riverdale Avenue; Conover Rd. is Valentine Street.
A lane lettered Private Road runs parallel to Park Road on the left.
Church of the Precious Blood: spire 70 ft, hot air heat, electric lights.
Beach Road at Ocean Avenue and at Railroad Avenue does not match the modern junctions within 9 to 14 m, so those junctions were left out of the fit.

Printed sheet 65, Monmouth Beach centre, scale 120 ft to an inch. Ocean Av., Railroad Av. (now Seaview Avenue), Cottage Rd., Beach Rd., River Av. and River Drive (now River Avenue), Club House Circle (now Club Circle), Park Rd. (Gull St.) (now West Street), Fresh Pond Rd. (now Riverdale Avenue), Surf Rd., Conover Rd. (now Valentine Street). One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 66 covers the southern end of Monmouth Beach down to the Long Branch city line at 60 feet to an inch, twice the scale of the neighbouring sheets, and is turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. Ocean Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally with a row of large cottages on its ocean side and the shore of the Atlantic Ocean above them; below it the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs parallel. Between the railroad and Ocean Avenue are smaller lots with dwellings and stables, numbered 1701 to 1720 and 1721 to 1740 along the avenue. Conover Road runs up the left edge, with lots numbered from the sheet 65 side, and Fresh Pond Road runs across the foot of the sheet, its lots numbered 1 to 30. The line of the City of Long Branch limits follows the south side of Fresh Pond Road, and Columbia Avenue, drawn with dashed edges, leaves it near the lower right towards sheet 61. A few houses of Long Branch appear below Fresh Pond Road, including an auto house and dwellings with distances to the nearest frame dwelling. A brown stain covers part of the bottom centre of the sheet. Block numbers 142 to 144 are printed, with a scale bar of 60 feet to one inch at the lower right.
notes: Renamed since: Conover Rd. is Valentine Street; Fresh Pond Rd. is Riverdale Avenue.
Modern Ocean Avenue lies about 15 to 20 m landward of the drawn Ocean Av. on this sheet.
Placed from two hand-picked junctions only (helmert); Columbia Av. is drawn dashed, perhaps as a proposed street.

Printed sheet 66, Monmouth Beach south end to the Long Branch city limits, scale 60 ft to an inch, turned on the page (north to the upper left, about -65 degrees). Ocean Av., Conover Rd. (now Valentine Street), Fresh Pond Rd. (now Riverdale Avenue), Columbia Av. (drawn dashed), Central R.R. of N.J. A stain covers the bottom centre. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: The left strip of sheet 67 continues sheet 64 northward into the southern end of Sea Bright, drawn at 120 feet to an inch in a long narrow band. Ocean Avenue runs up the strip with house numbers 2101 to 2149, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs parallel to it on the river side. East of Ocean Avenue, facing the Atlantic Ocean, are large cottages of H. Corn, J. H. Rhoades, W. N. Cromwell, J. N. Cornell, W. D. Walbridge, J. H. Haskell and the Estate of Dr. Tuck, and St. Peters Episcopal Church with its tower near the foot. West of the avenue stand the cottages of J. H. Skilling and B. A. Van Brunt. Below the key map the strip widens to the South Shrewsbury River, where the B. A. Van Brunt estate has a dwelling, wagon house, green house and heater house, store house, auto house, shed, a transformer house and boat houses along the winding shore. Block numbers 161 and 162 are printed. The top left of the sheet holds a small key map of Sea Bright, which is not part of this map; the sheet title and scale note are inside it.
notes: No street junction is drawn: placed from a point carried from sheet 64 at the match line and a point on modern Ocean Avenue 914 m north of it, the distance taken from the drawn scale. Low confidence.
The railroad has been removed; Ocean Avenue is the only street that survives.

Printed sheet 67, Sea Bright south end (Low Moor), scale 120 ft to an inch. Two strips side by side divided by a heavy double line: part 1 left strip (continues sheet 64 at its foot), part 2 right strip (continues the left strip at its foot, sheet 68 at its head). Only Ocean Av. and the railroad are drawn; no cross streets. Top-left key map of Sea Bright (sheets 64, 67-71) masked out.

sheet-4-2.description: The right strip of sheet 67 continues the left strip northward through the southern part of Sea Bright toward sheet 68, again at 120 feet to an inch. Ocean Avenue runs up the middle of the strip with house numbers 2201 to 2272, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs beside it on the west, with Low Moor Station near the foot. West of the railroad a narrow arm of the South Shrewsbury River reaches up the strip, with a few boat houses, an auto house and a bridge over the water. East of Ocean Avenue, facing the Atlantic Ocean, stands a row of large cottages: W. E. Conners, John L. Riker, the Estate of E. Fleitmann, W. J. Riker, Saml Riker, Houlser, W. I. Walker, J. A. Scrymser, C. S. Baylis and J. N. Cornell. Smaller dwellings and stables line the west side of the avenue. Block numbers 161 and 162 are printed again on this strip, and a compass rose sits on the double line dividing it from the left strip.
notes: No street junction is drawn: placed from points carried from the left strip at the match line and a point on modern Ocean Avenue 890 m north of it, the distance taken from the drawn scale. Low confidence.
Low Moor Station of the Central R.R. of N.J. stood near the foot of the strip; the railroad has been removed.

Printed sheet 67, Sea Bright south end (Low Moor), scale 120 ft to an inch. Two strips side by side divided by a heavy double line: part 1 left strip (continues sheet 64 at its foot), part 2 right strip (continues the left strip at its foot, sheet 68 at its head). Only Ocean Av. and the railroad are drawn; no cross streets. Top-left key map of Sea Bright (sheets 64, 67-71) masked out.
